chunks: Mansur ibn Yunus narrated from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said:

Isa ibn Musa, with Ibn Shubrumah beside him, asked me about a slain person found in the land of a people, with no one else there. So I said: The Ansar found a man in one of the irrigation channels of Khaybar. The Ansar said: 'The Jews killed our companion.' The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to them: 'Do you have evidence?' They said: 'No.' He said: 'Will you then swear?' The Ansar said: 'How can we swear to what we did not see?' He said: 'Then the Jews shall swear.' The Ansar said: 'Will they swear concerning our companion?' He said: So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم paid his blood-money from his own side. Then Ibn Shubrumah said: 'What do you think, had the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم not paid it?' He said: I said: 'We do not speak concerning what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم has done by saying: had he not done it.'
He said: So I said to him: 'Then upon whom is the qasamah?' He said: 'Upon the family of the slain person.'

key_terms.أَ فَتُقْسِمُونَ: will you swear; referring to taking an oath in legal procedure
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقَتِيلِ: the family of the slain person, upon whom the qasamah falls here
key_terms.الْقَتِيلِ: the slain or murdered person at the center of the legal case
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةُ: the formal oath procedure used in homicide cases
key_terms.خَيْبَرَ: Khaybar, the location mentioned in the reported case
key_terms.فَوَدَاهُ: he paid the blood-money or compensation for him

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, upon whom does the qasamah fall in a murder case with no direct evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of qasamah in a murder case where a slain person is found among a people without direct proof. It recalls the judgment of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in the Khaybar case and concludes that the qasamah falls upon the family of the murdered person.
